name: The Vitreous Banks
description:
A three-kilometer stretch of reclaimed Lake Michigan shoreline north of the old Evanston boundary where centuries of industrial glass waste, slag dumping, and subsequent geological pressure have fused the lakebed shallows into vast planes of cloudy, greenish sea-glass. At low water cycles — when the lake's managed sluice gates drop the shoreline level — the exposed flats catch GLMZ's tower-glow and scatter it in thousands of fractured directions, creating an eerie, beautiful light field visible from Spire observation decks on clear nights.

The Vitreous Banks are officially designated an environmental remediation zone under a dormant Palladian Group land-use agreement, which has kept heavy development at bay while simultaneously preventing any legitimate community from establishing permanent roots. In practice, the Banks host a transient population of salvagers, off-grid artists, and Tier 1 refugees who've built precarious stilt settlements in the shallows, trading in sea-glass artifacts, filtered lake water, and whatever bioelectric components wash ashore from Zheng-Dao's offshore processing platforms.

sights: Vast shallow flats of fused greenish glass glowing with refracted megacity light at dusk
Rickety stilt platforms connected by rope bridges and salvaged composite walkways
Zheng-Dao offshore rigs blinking red on the horizon through lake-haze
sounds: Glass fragments grinding and clicking softly as wave action shifts the shallows
Wind carrying distorted Diaspora signal fragments from poorly shielded stilt-community uplinks
The low foghorn cycling of lake traffic management buoys marking the shipping exclusion zone
smells: Cold lake water with a faint chemical sweetness from dissolved industrial mineral residue
Woodsmoke and recycled cooking oil from the stilt settlement cook-fires
Ozone and hot metal when Zheng-Dao's offshore platforms vent processing exhaust
atmosphere.feel: The Vitreous Banks feel like the end of something — a place where the city's momentum finally runs out against the water. There's genuine beauty here that sits uneasily alongside desperation, and the silence between wave cycles is the kind that makes people confess things.

demographics: Almost entirely Tier 1 and the Gray Zone-adjacent residents, with a small rotating population of off-grid artists, environmental surveyors working covert contracts, and salvagers of indeterminate affiliation.
economy: Subsistence-level barter economy centered on sea-glass artifact sales to Spire collectors, filtered water trading, and salvage recovery of Zheng-Dao bioelectric components that wash ashore from platform discharge.
power_structure: No formal authority; the largest stilt settlement cluster, called the Raft Council, mediates disputes informally, but Palladian Group's dormant land claim means any serious conflict invites corporate legal enforcement.
dangers: Glass flats fracturing without warning under foot traffic, especially after storm-driven wave cycles shift subsurface pressure
Zheng-Dao security drones sweeping the shore for unauthorized recovery of platform discharge components
Palladian Group periodically activating its land-use claim to displace settlements when development interest resurfaces
opportunities: Recovering high-value Zheng-Dao bioelectric components from shoreline discharge before corporate salvage crews arrive
Accessing the Banks' unique position outside Ferrogate Security jurisdiction for meetings that cannot happen inside the corridor
Finding Palladian Group's original remediation survey data, which locals claim is buried in a waterproofed archive beneath the oldest stilt platform
story_hooks: A Spire-tier art collector has been quietly purchasing every sea-glass artifact coming out of the Banks through three layers of intermediaries, and the prices have tripled in six months. Someone on the Raft Council suspects the collector isn't buying art — they're buying something that's embedded in specific pieces, and salvagers are starting to disappear when they ask too many questions.

Zheng-Dao Bioelectric has filed an emergency activation of the dormant Palladian land-use agreement, giving the stilt settlements forty-eight hours to vacate. The Raft Council is convinced it's connected to something their salvagers recovered from a platform discharge three weeks ago — a canister that nobody will describe in detail but that everyone on the council has seen.
frequented_by: Tier 1 salvagers and subsistence settlers building lives outside the corridor's formal economy
Off-grid artists and Diaspora-disconnected individuals seeking anonymity from BCI tracking infrastructure
Zheng-Dao Bioelectric covert recovery teams operating without corporate identification
Palladian Group legal surveyors quietly reassessing the land-use claim's development potential
